title: Marcianus graecus Z. 299 (=584): Corpus of the Greek Alchemists
shelf_note: The text belongs in the Greek alchemical corpus: it is Olympiodorus' commentary quoting Zosimos to Theosebeia, then Agathodaimon, Hermes and magnesia. But the leaf is in a fluent late cursive hand in brown ink, which does not look like the 10th–11th-century minuscule of Marc. gr. 299. This may be a later copy catalogued under the Marcianus. I am an expert-eye reader at this resolution only, so this is a doubt, not a finding (possible I7).
structure_note: pages_translated is 0 in the structure counts but 397 in the book field, so one of the two counts is wrong (E2). There are 199 printed numbers with 10 backsteps and 10 repeats. On a foliated manuscript (this leaf carries '169' in pencil, top and foot) that most likely comes from recto-only foliation being read onto versos, or from foliation misreads, not from a scan disorder. I have not confirmed this from one page.

pages.layout: single column of cursive Greek on a recto with a wide blank outer margin; pencil foliation '169' top right and at the foot; a strip of the facing verso's text at the left edge (correctly not transcribed)

ocr_errors.ocr: ὅταν δὲ ἐπιμείνας αὐτὴν. τό γε ἐπίγνωσιν καὶ τὸ μόνον
ocr_errors.image: ὅταν δὲ ἐπιγνῷς σαυτήν· τότε ἐπιγνώσῃ καὶ τὸν μόνον
ocr_errors.problem: 'when you know yourself, then you will know the only true God' is misread as 'persisting in it ... knowledge'; the key self-knowledge clause is lost
'spitting on matter' is read as 'loving what is yours', which reverses the sense

ocr_errors.ocr: καθίζου δὲ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἐν μηδὲ
ocr_errors.problem: 'sit still also as to the passions' is read as 'these same things in nothing'; the passions are lost
the motto 'One is the All' is misread, and the next line ('δι' οὗ τὸ πᾶν') becomes 'λόντι πᾶν'

ocr_errors.ocr: τοῦτο γὰρ ἡμῖν δεῖ τὸ πᾶν. οὐ δὲν τὸ πᾶν.
ocr_errors.image: τοῦτο γὰρ εἰ μὴ ἔχοι τὸ πᾶν, οὐδέν [ἐστι] τὸ πᾶν
ocr_errors.problem: a conditional ('if it did not hold the all, the all is nothing') is turned into a flat statement
a 'star' is invented where the leaf reads 'seeking'; the reading is uncertain at this resolution

ocr_errors.ocr: τὸ ἅγιον. καὶ οὕτως ἥξει πρὸς τὸ ἅγιον
ocr_errors.image: τὸ θεῖον· καὶ ὄντως ἥξει … τὸ θεῖον
ocr_errors.problem: 'the divine' is read as 'the holy', and ὄντως as οὕτως

ocr_errors.ocr: ἐνεργοῦσα ἐπὶ τούτῳ καὶ τὸν γνήσιον
ocr_errors.image: ἐνεργοῦσα ἐπιτεύξῃ τῶν γνησίων καὶ φυσικῶν
ocr_errors.problem: 'you will obtain the genuine and natural [tinctures]' is misread
'with regard to divine things' is misread

ocr_errors.ocr: ὁ γὰρ καπνός ἐστιν ἐξ ἀτμοῦ
ocr_errors.image: ὁ γὰρ καπνὸς … ἀτμοῦ θερ-|μοῦ καὶ ξηροῦ
ocr_errors.problem: 'θερ-' is dropped, so 'hot and dry vapour' becomes 'from vapour and from the dry'

tr_errors.source: καὶ ἀγαπῶσα τῆς ὑμετέρας (image: καταπτύουσα τῆς ὕλης)
tr_errors.problem: it carries the OCR misread, so a reader gets the opposite of 'spitting on matter'

tr_errors.source: ὅταν δὲ ἐπιμείνας αὐτὴν (image: ὅταν δὲ ἐπιγνῷς σαυτήν)
tr_errors.english: And when you have persisted in it, that is, in knowledge
tr_errors.problem: 'when you know yourself' is lost; the argument of the passage is changed

tr_errors.source: ἐν τῷ παν-|λόντι πᾶν … οὐ δὲν τὸ πᾶν (image: ἓν τὸ πᾶν … εἰ μὴ ἔχοι τὸ πᾶν, οὐδέν τὸ πᾶν)
tr_errors.problem: the 'One is the All' motto is unrecognisable, and the conditional becomes the flat claim 'the all is nothing'

tr_errors.english: so that no star flows out from it
tr_errors.problem: the English is fluent prose built on an invented reading; there is no star on the leaf

tr_errors.source: καθίζου δὲ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἐν μηδὲ
tr_errors.english: Sit, then, with these same things in nothing
tr_errors.problem: the sentence is meaningless and the passions (τοῖς πάθεσι) are lost; it is translated with no uncertainty marker

missing.why: In Greek alchemy 'magnesia' is a named substance or stage of the work, not the modern element or mineral. It is left with no gloss.

missing.english: For Hermes too speaks about the smoke
missing.why: A general reader needs to know this is Hermes Trismegistus as an alchemical authority.
The speaker and addressee are not identified (Zosimos quoted, writing to Theosebeia), so the quoted instructions are hard to follow.
This is Zosimos of Panopolis, the alchemist the passage relies on; one line naming him would help.

book_verdict: A Greek alchemical page (Olympiodorus quoting Zosimos) whose OCR misreads the hand at the points the argument turns on: 'know yourself', 'spitting on matter', 'One is the All'. The fluent English carries those misreads to the reader as sense. Its notes are mostly harmless transliterations. The 10th–11th-century catalogue date looks doubtful for this hand.
